target_customer: Mid sized and large Latin American enterprises with recurring billing, such as insurers, schools, utilities, telecoms and real estate firms
problem: Companies in Latin America collect recurring revenue across fragmented payment methods and lose revenue to failed payments, manual reminders and reconciliation.
business_model: B2B SaaS and payment collection platform, per volume or subscription
product_category: Accounts receivable and recurring payments platform

founders.name: Cristina Etcheberry
prior_employers: Latin America's largest airline (Latam Airlines, per DF), over three years
education: Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile, BS in Business and Economics
founders.background_notes: Self taught developer per YC page; named Product Manager on the YC page and CEO in the 2023 and 2025 press releases.

founders.name: Francisca Noguera
prior_employers: Falabella (three years in the Chilean financial market, Banco Falabella)
education: Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile, BS in Business and Economics
founders.background_notes: Per DF she stayed at the bank until the startup had traction.

founders.name: Enzo Tamburini
founders.background_notes: Chilean Python developer per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with ERPs, banks and local payment rails across several countries is standard but integration heavy work; compliance such as PCI DSS added later.

defensibility.rationale: Deep ERP and bank integrations plus local rails like Mexico's SPEI and Brazil's Pix are slow to replicate across countries.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company scaled to over 450 enterprise clients by 2025 and a Series A of about $48M.

market_need_then: Tool use for subscriptions and recurring collections was growing in Latin America; the company reportedly managed about US$3M per month at the time of its 2021 YC selection (Descubre, 2021-07-28).

branding.domain_note: Uses trytoku.com, a prefixed domain, per the company site.

identity.logo: Lavender accent (#AA90FE) per the site icon
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, enterprise oriented Spanish on the Chile site

branding.community_and_virality: Press attention to a women founded Latin American startup that raised the most capital in Chile (DF, 2024); no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Short distinctive name known in Latin American fintech press, though it uses a prefixed domain and no brand assets drew attention.

pivots.from: Payment collection and reminders for subscriptions
pivots.to: Payments and AI agents for sales, support and collections for large enterprises
pivots.why: Company site now lists AI agents; reason and date not stated

outcome_analysis: Toku went from a YC Summer 2021 recurring payments startup to a 150 person company with over 450 enterprise clients, raising a $7.15M seed in 2023 and a Series A of $9.3M in 2024 extended by $38.7M in 2025. Enterprise sales focus, ERP and bank integrations and early traction explain the progress; no failure signs were found.
notes: Series A: first close $9.3M (April 2024), extension of $38.7M in April 2025; Pulse 2.0 and Business Wire call it a $48M Series A with $55M total. Seed headline says $7.15M while the body says $7M. A Spanish blog cites a valuation above $175M, which is unverified and not recorded. Pre 2021 funding not found (earlier investors FundersClub and Clocktower appear as existing in 2023). Competitor list empty: CB Insights lists Puntored, Fintoc and others without dates, and no source dated near the 2021 batch names rivals. Etcheberry is titled Product Manager on the YC page but CEO in releases.
